newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-CANADIANS TANGO WITH JUDGES.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-CANADIANS TANGO WITH JUDGES.

text.p: The dance competition at the world figure skating championships began on Tuesday with a waltz, a rhumba and a tango with the judges.

The Canadian pair of Shae-Lynn Bourne and Victor Kraatz, hoping to challenge the Russian domination of the event, left the ice in third place in the compulsory phase of the competition and promptly hit out at the judges.
"Look at the panel. The majority of judges are from the eastern bloc and then there's a few western judges and that creates a few of the problems," said Kraatz.
"I think if every judge were to just judge according to what they see, everything would be much better."
Ahead of the Canadians are two Russian pairs, Olympic and three-time world champions Evgeny Platov and Oksana Grishuk and Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov.

Third place was a major disappointment to Bourne and Kraatz, who now face an uphill battle if they are to repeat their gold medal success of a forntight ago when they beat Krylova and Ovsyannikov in the Champions Series final in Ontario.
They did, however, receive one first place vote for their efforts in the two compulsory dances and that, ironically, came from their own Canadian judge, John Greenwood, in the rhumba.
Even so, last year's bronze medallists considered that a major breakthrough.
"He (Greenwood) had the guts to finally do something about what's going on as far as skating goes," said Kraatz.
"He's not concerned so much about hierarchy. Finally things are turning in the right direction."
His partner, Bourne, was no less disappointed by the perceived old eastern bloc, Cold War allegiances but was upbeat about their one success.
"I'm thrilled. That was the greatest thing about our last dance," said Bourne. "I'm more thrilled about that one first than anything.
"It just shows each judge has a different opinion, and he's (Greenwood) a good judge -- an honest judge."
